messages:
maria (PM): Quick sync — we need a minimal, testable gating matrix for geo cutover + tenant isolation asks from AcmeCorp. I pulled together a draft. Feedback?

dylan (Eng): share the draft pls. are we talking canary + staged traffic shift?

maria (PM): yes. proposal: 1) staging canary (single tenant slice), 2) gated 5% prod traffic for 24h, 3) roll to 50% then 100% if signals green. gating signals below.

jon (Arch): add one more gate: cold-start p95 for model variants when KV cache miss rate spikes. we saw regressions in q3.

priya (SRE): agree. also require automated fallback policy in place before canary: fallback to regional-compatible smaller model, and circuit-breaker on sustained errors.

alex (Sales): Acme specifically asked for cross-region failover within 30s and SLA for tail latency. they will push contract language. can we quantify?

maria (PM): proposed launch signals (binary/pass thresholds):
- p99 latency (end-user) < 120ms on regional requests
- error rate < 0.5% (5xx + model failures)
- regional failover recovery time < 30s
- KV cache warmup < 2 minutes for pinned tenants
- no customer-visible consistency regressions in top-10 prompts
(we can make numbers looser if ops flags concerns)

dylan (Eng): p99 120ms seems aggressive for cross-region. for some model sizes we should have model-variant routing: default -> quantized variant when under pressure. that must be in playbook.

jon (Arch): policy idea: SLA-triggered affinity. if a tenant breaches p99 > 200ms for >5 minutes, automatically move them to an affinity lane (isolated slice) and notify CD. document migration window.

priya (SRE): operational acceptance: enable the following before canary:
- automated alert set: "region.failover.latency"
- runbook for manual evacuation and slice pinning
- smoke test harness that runs top-20 prompts every 15m
If any fail -> rollback.

alex (Sales): customer will accept canary but wants a rollback SLA: if we roll back, they expect no more than 1 minute of increased error surface for their tenant. is that realistic?

dylan (Eng): 1 minute window unrealistic for some migrations, but we can commit to automatic traffic cutover within 60s if fallback policy triggers. full restoration depends on cache warmup. be explicit in contract.

maria (PM): okay let's capture conservative contract language: "automated failover within 60s to compatible model variant; expected full performance restoration within 10 minutes under normal load".

jon (Arch): launch checklist (minimal):
- routing policy versioned and testable in sandbox
- canary automation (traffic shaping + rollback)
- fallback variants configured and vetted
- telemetry: per-tenant p50/p95/p99, cache hit ratio, failover events
- runbook + SLO docs for customer success

priya (SRE): add chaos window test: simulate regional outage during canary to validate failover. do it with one internal tenant first.

maria (PM): timeline suggestion: prototype gating matrix + infra changes in sprint 2; internal pilot in sprint 3; customer pilot (Acme) in sprint 4 if pilot metrics pass.

alex (Sales): Acme will likely want pilot in 6 weeks. can we accelerate pilot to sprint 3 if we scope pilot to 2 tenants only?

dylan (Eng): possible if we narrow model sizes and disable cross-region routing for pilot. reduces blast radius.

jon (Arch): must add acceptance signal: regression run against our baseline prompts with automated BLEU/embedding-similarity check and manual QA sign-off.

maria (PM): agreed. action items: @dylan draft routing policy PR with canary hooks; @priya add runbook + chaos test plan; @jon write acceptance signal checklist; @alex confirm contractual wording with Acme and drop into thread. I'll collate and create gating matrix doc.

ops-bot: Created #ticket-1234 to track geo-cutover-gating. Assigned to dylan, priya, jon, maria. ETA: 2025-07-11.

alex (Sales): noted. I'll push for pilot window and share Acme's legal language. :thumbsup:

maria (PM): thanks all — I’ll publish the first draft gating matrix by EOD and ping for final technical signoff.
